questions.question: At a certain sum of money with the interest rate of 6% per annum for 4 years. the simple interest is Rs. 4500. Find the compound interest (compounding annually) of 2 years at the same sum when the rate of interest is 4% per annum,
questions.questionHtml: At a certain sum of money with the interest rate of 6% per annum for 4 years. the simple interest is Rs. 4500. Find the compound interest (compounding annually) of 2 years at the same sum when the rate of interest is 4% per annum,
questions.solution:
Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100 ⇒ 4500 = (P × 6 × 4)/100 ⇒ P = Rs. 18750

Compound Interest = P(1 + R/100)T - P ⇒ 18750(1 + 4/100)2 - 18750 = 1530

questions.question: What is the present value of the sum if the interest compounded at the rate of 18% per annum for two years is Rs. 981?
questions.questionHtml: What is the present value of the sum if the interest compounded at the rate of 18% per annum for two years is Rs. 981?
questions.solution:
Let the present value is 100

After 1 yr it would be 118

Then after 2 yr the value is 118 × 18/100 = 21.24

Total interest received in two years 21.24 + 18 = 39.24

As per the question,

value of 39.24 = 981

So value of 100 units = 981/39.24 × 100

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 9500 amounts to Rs. 11495 in 2 years at a certain rate percent per annum, interest compounded yearly. What is the simple interest (in Rs. ) on the same sum for the same time and double the rate?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of Rs. 9500 amounts to Rs. 11495 in 2 years at a certain rate percent per annum, interest compounded yearly. What is the simple interest (in Rs. ) on the same sum for the same time and double the rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amount = Rs. 11495

Principal = Rs. 9500

Time = 2 years

Formula used:

A = P(1 + r/100)t

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Calculation:

A = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 11495 = 9500(1 + r/100)2

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = (11495/9500)

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = (121/100)

⇒ (1 + r/100)2 = (11/10)2

⇒ r = 10%

Now,

According to the question

Principal = Rs. 9500

Rate = double the rate = (2 × 10) = 20%

Time = 2 years

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ Rs. (9500 × 20 × 2)/100

⇒ Rs. (95 × 20 × 2)

⇒ Rs. 3800

∴ The required SI is Rs. 3800

questions.question: Find the amount if a sum of Rs. 7,500 is invested on compound interest at 8% p.a. for 1.5 years when the interest is compounded half yearly.
questions.questionHtml: Find the amount if a sum of Rs. 7,500 is invested on compound interest at 8% p.a. for 1.5 years when the interest is compounded half yearly.

options.html: Rs. 8,657.48

questions.solution:
Given:

Principle = Rs. 7,500

Rate of interest = 8%

n = 1.5 years 

Concept Used:

A = P(1 + \(\frac{R}{100}\))n

Where, P = Principle, A = Amount, R = Rate of interest

Calculation:

⇒ P1 = Rs. 7,500 

⇒ R for half year = 4%

⇒ So, the amount after 1/2 year = P(1 + \(\frac{R}{100}\)) = 7500(1 + \(\frac{4}{100}\)) = 7800

⇒ P2 = Rs. 7,800 and R = 4%

⇒ Amount after 1 year =  P(1 + \(\frac{R}{100}\)) = 7800(1 + \(\frac{4}{100}\)) = 8112

⇒ P3 = Rs. 8,112 and R = 4%

⇒ Amount after 1.5 year = P(1 + \(\frac{R}{100}\)) = 8112(1 + \(\frac{4}{100}\)) = 8436.48

⇒ Hence Amount = Rs. 8,436.48

Therefore, the amount after the investment for 1.5 years at the rate of 8% is Rs. 8,436.48.

questions.question: In how many years will a sum of Rs 800 become Rs 1216.70 at 30% per annum compounding half-yearly?
questions.questionHtml: In how many years will a sum of Rs 800 become Rs 1216.70 at 30% per annum compounding half-yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:

Type = Compound

Principle = Rs. 800

Rate = 30%

Amount = Rs.1216.70

Formula used:

A = P x [1 + (R /100)]T

A = CI + P

here, 

A = Amount

CI = Compound Interest

P = Principle

R = Rate

T = Time

Solution:

Let's put the values given, in the formula to find the value of T;

R = 30/2 = 15% for half year

1216.7 = 800[1 + 15/100]T

1216.7 = 800 x 1.15T

1.15T = 1216.7/800 = 1.520875

1.15T = 1.153 

Hence, T = 3.

It was compounded half yearly, so, total time in years = 3/2 = 1.5 years.

Hence, it will require 1.5 years.

questions.question: At what rate percentage per annum will ₹14,400 amount to ₹15,876 in one year, if interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.questionHtml: At what rate percentage per annum will ₹14,400 amount to ₹15,876 in one year, if interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 14,400

Amount = 15,876

Time = 1 year

Concept:

when interest in compounded half yearly, then time is multiplied by 2 and rate is divided by 2.

A = P(1 + r/100)t

where A, P, r and t are amount, principal, rate and time respectively.

Calculation:

Time = 2 (i.,e. 1 × 2)

15,876 = 14,400(1 + r/100)2

⇒ 15,876/14,400 = (1 + r/100)2

⇒ √15,876/√14,400 = (1 + r/100)

⇒ 126/120 = (1 + r/100)

⇒ 126/120 = 1 + r/100

⇒ 126/120 = (100 + r)/100

⇒ (126 × 100)/120 = 100 + r

⇒ 105 = 100 + r

⇒ 105 - 100 = r

⇒ 5% = r

As, interest is compounded half yearly. So,rate will be double 10%. (i.e. 5 × 2).

∴ Rate of interest is 10% .

questions.question: The compound interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 12,000 at 10% per annum for 1.5 years, interest compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 12,000 at 10% per annum for 1.5 years, interest compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A sum = Rs. 12,000

Rate = 10% per annum

And time = 1.5 years.

Formula used:

Amount = Principal{1 + (R/100)}n

Where n = time in years and R = rate percentage/annum

Compund interest = Amount - Principal

If time = n years, rate = R% and interest compounded half-yearly

Then time = 2n  and rate = (R/2)%

Calculation:

Interest compounded half-yearly:

Then time = 2 × 1.5

⇒ 3 years

And the rate = 10/2

⇒ 5% 

Amount = 12000 × {1 + (5/100)}3

⇒ 12000 × {1 + (1/20)}3

⇒ 12000 × {(20 + 1)/20}3

⇒ 12000 × (21/20)3

⇒ 12000 × (9261/8000)

⇒ 12 × 9261/8

⇒ 1,11,132/8

⇒ Rs. 13891.5

Compound interest = amount - principal

⇒ 13891.5 - 12000

⇒ Rs. 1891.5

∴ The compound interest is Rs. 1891.5

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest (in Rs.) compounded yearly and compounded half yearly for 18 months at 20% per annum on a sum of Rs. 12,000?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference between the compound interest (in Rs.) compounded yearly and compounded half yearly for 18 months at 20% per annum on a sum of Rs. 12,000?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal amount = Rs. 12000

Time = 18 months

Rate of interest = 20%

Concept used:

Simple interest = (Principal × Time × Rate) ÷ 100

In the case of compound interest,

A = P × (1 + r/100)n

C.I = A - P

Here, A = Amount, P = Principal, r = Rate of interest. n = Time, C.I = Compound interest

Calculation:

When interest is compounded yearly,

Principal = Rs. 12,000

At the end of the first year, the principal becomes = 12000 × 1.21 = Rs. 14400

Then, after 6 months the interest accumulated on the principal amount of Rs. 14400

⇒ (14400 × 20 × 6/12) / 100

⇒ 1440

So, after 8 months the initial principal amount becomes = 14400 + 1440 = Rs. 15840

Interest accumuted in 18 months = Rs. (15840 - 12000) = Rs. 3840

When interest compounded half-yearly,

Rate of interest (R) = 20/2 % = 10%

Time (n) = 18 ÷ 6 = 3

Principal = 12,000

So, after 18 months the principal becomes

⇒ 12000 (1 + 10/100)3

⇒ Rs. 15972

Interest accumuted in 18 months = Rs. (15972 - 12000) = Rs. 3972

So, the difference between the interest accumulated = Rs. (3972 - 3840) = Rs. 132

∴ The difference between the compound interest compounded yearly and compounded half yearly for 18 months at 20% per annum on a sum of Rs. 12,000 is Rs. 132.

Alternate Method Formulae used:

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = P[(1 + (r/200))2n – (1 + (r/100))n]

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = 12000[(1 + (20/200))2(1.5) – (1 + (20/100))1.5]

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = 12000 [(1 + (1/10))3– (1 + (1/5))1.5]

CIhalf yearly – CIyearly = 132

questions.questionHtml: At a certain rate of interest compounded annually, a sum amounts to ₹10,890 in 2 years and to ₹11,979 in 3 years. The sum is:

GIVEN:

The sum amounts to Rs10,890 in 2 years

The sum amounts to Rs11,979 in 3 years

FORMULA USED:

Amount = \(P (1 +\frac{R}{100})^t\) 

where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, and t = time.

CALCULATION :

10,890 = P× \(( 1+\frac{R}{100})^2\)  ...............(1)

11,979 = P × \((1 + \frac{R}{100})^3\) ................(2)

On dividing Eq (2) by Eq(1) we get,

⇒ 1.1 = \(( 1 + \frac{R}{100})\) 

⇒ 0.1 = R/100  = 10

⇒ R = 10 p.a. 

Now put the value of R in eq1 we get,

⇒ 10,890 = P× \((1.1)^2\) 

⇒ P = 9000 .

⇒ The sum is Rs9000.

questions.question: A sum invested at compound interest amounts to Rs. 7,800 in 3 years and Rs. 11,232 in 5 years. What is the rate per cent?
questions.questionHtml: A sum invested at compound interest amounts to Rs. 7,800 in 3 years and Rs. 11,232 in 5 years. What is the rate per cent?
questions.solution:
Here, Rs. 7800 becomes Rs. 11232 at compound interest in two years. Let, the rate of interest = R

⇒ 11232 = \(7800\left(1+\frac{R}{100} \right)^2\) ⇒ [(100 + R)/100]2 = 11232/7800

⇒ [(100 + R)/100]2 = (12/10)2 ⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = (12/10)

Amount of A after 8 years = Amount of B after 10 years

⇒ PA[1 + R/100]8 = PB[1 + 10/100]1 ⇒ PA (11/10)8 = PB(11/10)10 ⇒ PA/PB = (11/10)2 = 121/100 ⇒ PA + PB = 121 + 100 = 221

According to the question, ⇒ 221 → 66,300 ⇒ 1 → 66,300/221 = 300. Hence, PA = 300 × 121 = 36,300 and PB = 300 × 100 = 30,000

∴ A's and B's share are Rs. 36,300 and Rs. 30,000.

questions.question: What is the compound interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 25,000 for 3 \(\frac{2}{5}\) years at 10% p.a, if the interest is compounded annually?

questions.solution:
Given:

A = P(1 + r/100)n

questions.question: Amir borrowed a sum of Rs. 25,000 on simple interest. Bhola borrowed the same amount on compound interest (interest compounded yearly). At the end of 2 years, Bhola had to pay Rs. 160 more interest than Amir. The rate of interest charged per annum is:
questions.questionHtml: Amir borrowed a sum of Rs. 25,000 on simple interest. Bhola borrowed the same amount on compound interest (interest compounded yearly). At the end of 2 years, Bhola had to pay Rs. 160 more interest than Amir. The rate of interest charged per annum is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) is: Difference = P × (R/100)2

160 = 25,000 × (R/100)2

160 = 25,000 × R2 / 10,000

160 = 2.5 × R2 ⇒ R2 = 64

R = 8%

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹25,000

Time (T) = 2 years

Interest Difference (CI − SI) = ₹160

Formula Used:

For 2 years, Difference (D) = P × (R/100)2

Calculations:

⇒ 160 = 25,000 × (R/100) × (R/100)

⇒ 160 = 25,000 × R2 / 10,000

⇒ 160 = 2.5 × R2

⇒ R2 = 160 / 2.5

⇒ R2 = 1600 / 25

⇒ R2 = 64

⇒ R = √64

⇒ R = 8

∴ The correct answer is 8%.

Additional Information

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is given by: D = P × (R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

Successive Interest Rates

For Compound Interest, if the rate for the 1st year is R1 and for the 2nd year is R2, the effective rate is (R1 + R2 + R1×R2/100)%.

SI vs CI for 1st Year

For the first year (if compounded annually), the Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always equal.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹ 10,000 for 1 \(1\over2\) years at 4% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference between the compound interest on ₹ 10,000 for 1\(1\over2\) years at 4% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principle amount of Rs. 10000 compounded for 1\(1\over2\) years at 4% per annum, yearly and half-yearly.

Formula used:

Present value = \(P\left( 1+ \frac{r}{100}\right)^{n}\), where P is the principle amount, r is the annual interest rate and n is time in years.

Calculation:

When compounded yearly: 

The value after first year = 10000(1 + 0.04)1 = 10400

The value after 1.5 years = 10400(1 + 0.5 × 0.04) = 10608

When compounded half-yearly, n = 1.5 × 2 = 3, r = 0.5 × 4 = 2%. 

The value after 1.5 years = 10000(1 + 2/100)3 = 10612.08

∴ The difference between the compound interest on ₹ 10,000 for 1\(1\over2\) years at 4% per annum compounded yearly and half-yearly is 10612.08 - 10608 = Rs. 4.08

questions.question: A certain sum is invested at 26% p.a, interest compounded annually. In how many years (approx) will it double?
questions.questionHtml: A certain sum is invested at 26% p.a, interest compounded annually. In how many years (approx) will it double?
questions.solution:
Given:- 

Interest rate(r) = 26% p.a.

Formula used:-

\(A = P\times\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}\)

Calculation:- 

Let the initial amount be X

It is given that interest is compounded annually which signifies that n = 1

It is mentioned that the interest is getting double,

Let after time 'T' the final amount will be 2X

By using formula of compound interest using n = 1,

⇒ \(2X=X\times \left(1+r\right)^{T}\)

⇒ \(2=\left(1+r\right)^{T}\)

Put the value of r = 26% in the equation,

⇒ \(2=(1.26)^{T}\)

Taking \(\log_{1.26}\) on both sides,

\(\log_{1.26}^{\ 2}\ =\ \log_{1.26}^{\ {(1.26)}^T}\)

⇒ \(\log_{1.26}^{\ 2} =T\)

T = 2.99 years

The total required to double the initial sum is 3 years(approx).
